searchText: <@488328812501663744> Please post whatever you learn here. I'm very curious if witness encryption is actually possible. Combining it with blockchain state transition functions, it opens a number of doors for some fancy stuff one could build on top of it. A simple example is that it simplifies commit-reveal schemes *greatly* from a UX standpoint. Rather than needing to first commit, then wait, then reveal you can instead commit a witness encrypted thing and then have it be revealed by bots after the triggering event occurs. My suspicion is that going from "it is theoretically possible to turn any function into a witness function" to "actually turning a full Ethereum client into a witness function" is a pretty huge leap though. iirc there was a construction based on multilinear maps but we don't have multilinear maps yet "We" meaning humanity? yeah Hmm, so it is purely theoretic at this point? unfortunately yeah ikr multilinear maps also gives us iO, which would make privacy *very* easy and *very* expressive ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ but guess we'll have to wait Can't we just point GPT-5 at the problem or something? 😬 Will do. I think treyzania is correct though.
